questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Browser API Integration”?
options: Browser API Integration helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Browser API Integration means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Browser API Integration removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Browser API Integration should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
questions.answer_key: Browser API Integration helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Browser API Integration is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Clipboard API” in this lesson?
options: Treat “Clipboard API” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Clipboard API” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Clipboard API” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Clipboard API” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Clipboard API” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Clipboard API” under Browser API Integration. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Browser API Integration”?
options: Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
